races.title: State Assembly, District 23
races.note: The top two finishers from the Nov 3, 2026 count. Everyone else in this race is coming.

cands.name: David G. Johnson
cands.bio: Santa Clara County native with 40 years in commercial construction (marketing, estimating, project management). Owns two small firms, started in 1994 and 2010. Chairman of the Santa Clara County Republican Party. Ran as a Republican for California State Assembly District 23 in 2026. Has held no prior elected office.

endorsements.text: Ballotpedia lists Reform California among his endorsements and voter-guide recommendations. It also lists The Morning Answer with Jennifer Horn and several informal voter guides (April's Common Sense Cali Voters, Based in Malibu, Elizabeth Barcohana's Lady with a Brain Voter Guide).

cands.gaps: We could not find his exact birthplace or hometown, his birth year, or his education; his Santa Clara County roots and career come only from his own campaign site. We found no independent reporting confirming his business history or his role as county Republican Party chair. He has held no public office, so there are no official actions to report. He did not complete Ballotpedia's candidate survey. We found no stated position from him on data centers, specific development or growth projects, homestead property tax relief, limits on investor or foreign land buying, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay, gun laws, or abortion. His site gives a general 'no more taxes' pledge until spending is fully transparent, and an idea to fund low-income housing with private money, but nothing that speaks directly to those topics. No controversies were found in the pages available.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign site says he is a 'proud, lifelong native of Santa Clara County' who has worked in the South Bay construction industry for 40 years; this is self-reported and not independently confirmed.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Has run two small construction-related firms since 1994 and 2010 and worked 40 years in commercial construction. Currently chairs the Santa Clara County Republican Party. No legislative, policy-staff or local elected experience was found.
qual.why: Business owner and manager background fits the middle band. There is no prior legislative service or budget or policy career to place him higher.
qual.label: Business owner and manager background fits the middle band. There is no prior legislative service or budget or policy career to place him higher.

school-choice-teachers.evidence: Says he will champion Parents' Rights and School Choice in Sacramento so families control education. His site names no specific voucher or charter bill and says nothing about teacher pay.

cands.name: Marc Berman
cands.bio: Democrat and attorney who has represented the San Francisco Peninsula and Silicon Valley in the California State Assembly since 2016. Earlier he served on the Palo Alto City Council. He worked at Latham & Watkins and Merino Yebri, LLP, and at the Silicon Valley Education Foundation.

endorsements.text: 2026 endorsements listed by Ballotpedia include the Democratic Party of California, California Teachers Association, SEIU Local 521, IUOE Local 3, National Union of Healthcare Workers, California Environmental Voters, Equality California and YIMBY Action.

In 2024 Berman listed endorsements from Gov. Gavin Newsom, Sen. Alex Padilla, Attorney General Rob Bonta, Planned Parenthood Advocates Mar Monte, the California Labor Federation and Sierra Club California.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions from Berman on data centers, homestead property tax elimination, limits on institutional or foreign buyers of homes and land, H-1B or immigration enforcement, police pay and pensions, or school vouchers and teacher pay. We found no record of when he moved to California, if he was not here from early childhood. He did not complete Ballotpedia's 2026 candidate survey, so his current self-described positions come from his 2024 survey and his campaign site. The campaign site's description of his bills was not checked against legislative records. We found no controversies in the pages provided.

local.label: Roots 90: Berman was born in Dallas, Texas, and raised in Palo Alto, where he graduated from Palo Alto High School, and he has since held office on the Palo Alto City Council and in the Assembly.

land.label: 1 documented position for data centers or more development

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: Assemblymember since 2016 (elections committee chair, later business and professions committee chair), former Palo Alto City Council member, and former attorney at Latham & Watkins and Merino Yebri, LLP, with a J.D. from USC.
qual.why: He has about ten years of prior legislative service plus local elected office and a legal career, which fits the high band for writing law and budgets. Committee chairs were not counted toward the score.
qual.label: He has about ten years of prior legislative service plus local elected office and a legal career, which fits the high band for writing law and budgets. Committee chairs were not counted toward the score.

pro-life.evidence: Berman says access to safe and legal abortion is a fundamental right and that he will protect access to birth control, abortion and reproductive healthcare. His campaign site says he was principal co-author of the constitutional amendment that became Proposition 1 in 2022.

slow-growth-protect-land.evidence: Berman says he has been a vocal advocate for building more housing across California. His campaign site says he authored AB 1804 (2018), a narrow CEQA exemption for multi-family and mixed-use infill housing in unincorporated areas.

second-amendment.evidence: Berman lists reducing gun violence as a policy priority. He says he authored a bill creating a firearm violence prevention training program for physicians.

roots.summary: Berman was born in Dallas, Texas, and raised in Palo Alto, where he graduated from Palo Alto High School, and he has since held office on the Palo Alto City Council and in the Assembly.

land_positions.quote_or_summary: In his 2024 Ballotpedia survey, Berman said he has been "a vocal advocate for the need to act responsibly and build more housing across California." Wikipedia also describes him as taking a pro-housing stance favoring production of housing.
